speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. I see you've been experiencing changes in behavior and eating habits, along with weight gain. To understand the cause, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male. The patient has demonstrated inappropriate behavior, including making unfitting comments and attempts to kiss strangers, over the past 6 months. He shows disinterest in family interactions and has developed a particular craving for chocolate pudding and potato chips, resulting in a 10 kg weight gain. The patient also presents as unkempt.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are you experiencing extreme thirst and frequent urination alongside these behavioral changes? Have you noticed any vision changes or confusion recently? REQUEST TEST: HbA1c, Fasting Glucose, TSH.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inappropriate behavior. I also have Disinterest in family interactions, Craving for specific foods, Significant weight gain, Apathy, Blunted affect. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cushing's Syndrome. The combination of central obesity, food cravings, apathy, inappropriate behavior, and the incorrect initial diagnosis of migraine strongly suggests chronic hypercortisolism rather than primary psychiatric or neurological issues.
